extracted.intended_audience: short-story authors, literary critics, editors, and informed readers of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical standards for assessing short stories, short-story collections, translations, and illustrated volumes (qualities such as characterization, imaginative power, translation fidelity, subtlety of irony, regional authenticity, realism, and lasting value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special excellence marker (asterisk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stones of special excellence are indicated by an asterisk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works marked with an asterisk are to be read/treated as having special excellence above the ordinary entries; the asterisk communicates an editorial judgment of outstanding quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: homely humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The homely humanity of his characterization’ (praise of Stacy Aumonier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong short story renders characters with a down-to-earth human quality that makes them recognizably real and sympathetic; characterization can be the central seat of a story's power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories show a ‘rich imaginative talent’ and expressiveness even in quiet modes of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imaginative resources — fresh images, original perspectives, or a distinctive imaginative voice — are a primary criterion; even subtle or domestic material should exhibit imaginative richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic intention subordinate to artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘He has a certain didactic intention in these stories, he has kept it entirely subordinate to the artistry of his exposition.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral or instructive aims are acceptable but should not overwhelm artistic technique; strong stories allow any lesson to arise organically from craft rather than preach overtly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability and economy of characters
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is the few characters which he has added to English fiction that we remember after his somewhat obvious moral has been conveyed.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short fiction benefits from economical casts in which a small number of well-rendered characters remain memorable after the story ends; avoid unneeded character proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation fidelity to imaginative style
rubrics_metrics.description: Translators should ‘succeed in reflecting successfully the fine imaginative style of this prose poem’ (praise of the translators of Apukhtin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For translated short stories, priority is given to rendering the author's imaginative voice and stylistic nuance into the target language; successful translation preserves tone and imaginative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and suitability of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections can be ‘superbly illustrated with many pictures ... these pictures are indescribable, but they will rejoice the heart of any child.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should match the book's tone and audience and enhance the reader's experience; outstanding artwork can be an integral component of a collection's success, especially for younger readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic/lyric quality and thematic depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Works described as a ‘poetic study in life after death’ or similar have a strong lyric or poetic element that deepens theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short stories that adopt a poetic tone or approach complex themes poetically are valued for depth and resonance; reviewers prize successful fusion of narrative and lyricism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological revelation and mordant self-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories with a ‘quality of bitter irony and mordant self-analysis’ and whose ‘psychological revelation of the mind ... is complete’ are praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psychological insight — candid, even harsh, exploration of inner states — is a mark of excellence; courageous, unflinching dissections of character and motive, even when appalling, can be judged healthfully truthful and important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with an author's established strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: A volume may be commended if it ‘adequately maintained the quality of his best previous ... work.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical appraisal considers whether a new collection sustains or advances an author's known strengths (style, themes, technique); consistency or growth is a positive sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of imaginative world
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for writers who ‘found a new imaginative world’ (e.g., Blackwood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality of setting, conceit, or imaginative premise — the creation of a new imaginative world — is a distinguishing criterion: inventiveness that yields fresh reader experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative beauty and potential for lasting poignancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that ‘serve the same altar of beauty’ and whose ‘magic will gain greater poignancy as generations pass’ are highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic beauty in language and conception and the ability to endure emotionally over time are signs of a work's lasting literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form suitability (short story as the right medium)
rubrics_metrics.description: The short story may be ‘her true literary medium’ (the form best suited to the writer's gifts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics assess whether the chosen form (short story, novella, novel) is the most effective vehicle for the material and the author's talents; mismatch between form and material is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety of irony
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘A subtle irony pervades them ... so definitely concealed that its insistence is never evident.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony that is skillfully concealed and understated — not blatant or heavy-handed — is praised; subtle irony that enriches rather than dominates the narrative is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional authenticity and dramatic vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for ‘racy humor ... vivid dramatic power’ and being ‘the first adequate imaginative interpreter of the people’ (regional representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic depiction of local color, dialect, customs, and vivid dramatic presentation that convincingly evoke a region or people are valued; successful regional writing combines fidelity with imaginative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid, unflinching realism (brutal power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that ‘portray the naked ugliness of warfare, and the passions which warfare engenders, with more brutal power’ are ranked highly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unvarnished, forceful realism that captures harsh truths (e.g., of war) can be a major virtue; reviewers may accept appalling realism when it is truthful and artistically controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelessness / enduring appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Works described as ‘destined never to grow old’ (timelessness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion is whether a story or collection appears likely to retain interest and value across time; enduring human themes, depth, and artistry contribute to timelessness.
